# 1. Executive Summary

This report analyzes historical retail demand and evaluates three forecasting models: Moving Average, Exponential Smoothing and ARIMA.

# 2. Load Forecasting Results

```{r setup, include=FALSE} id="j4up0a"
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

model_comparison <- read.csv("../reports/fair_forecast_model_comparison.csv")

forecast_7 <- read.csv("../reports/demand_forecast_7_days.csv")
forecast_30 <- read.csv("../reports/demand_forecast_30_days.csv")
forecast_90 <- read.csv("../reports/demand_forecast_90_days.csv")
```

# 3. Forecast Model Comparison

```{r} id="q99k6p"
kable(model_comparison, digits = 2)
```

# 4. Model Performance Visualization

```{r} id="d3vjj2"
ggplot(model_comparison, aes(x = Model, y = RMSE, fill = Model)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "Forecast Model Comparison - RMSE",
    x = "Forecasting Model",
    y = "Root Mean Squared Error"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

# 5. Seven-Day Demand Forecast

```{r} id="v5l6v1"
kable(forecast_7, digits = 2)

ggplot(forecast_7, aes(x = as.Date(Date), y = Predicted_Demand)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "darkorange") +
  labs(
    title = "Seven-Day Demand Forecast",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Predicted Demand"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 6. Thirty-Day Demand Forecast

```{r} id="3g88fh"
ggplot(forecast_30, aes(x = as.Date(Date), y = Predicted_Demand)) +
  geom_line(color = "darkgreen") +
  labs(
    title = "Thirty-Day Demand Forecast",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Predicted Demand"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 7. Ninety-Day Demand Forecast

```{r} id="jpp3be"
ggplot(forecast_90, aes(x = as.Date(Date), y = Predicted_Demand)) +
  geom_line(color = "purple") +
  labs(
    title = "Ninety-Day Demand Forecast",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Predicted Demand"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 8. Key Findings

- Three forecasting models were evaluated using MAE, RMSE and MAPE.
- Exponential Smoothing achieved the lowest error across the three evaluation metrics.
- Moving Average and ARIMA were also evaluated as comparison models.
- Forecasts were generated for 7, 30 and 90 days.

# 9. Business Recommendations

1. Use demand forecasts as a planning guide.
2. Monitor demand patterns before replenishing inventory.
3. Review forecasting accuracy when new sales data becomes available.
4. Consider seasonal patterns when planning stock levels.

# 10. Conclusion

The forecasting analysis demonstrates how time-series models can support retail demand planning and inventory decisions.

**Data Limitation:** The historical dataset covers December 2009 to December 2011. Forecast dates are historical projections after the final dataset date, not predictions for the current year. Forecasts are based on international Online Retail II data, not live Kerala sales.
